identityReview: Hanan Ashrawi (حنان عشراوي), born 8 October 1946 in Nablus to a Ramallah family, Palestinian scholar, politician and civil-rights advocate. Her 1991–1993 spokesperson role, 1996–1998 ministry, 1996/2006 PLC elections and 2009/2018 PLO executive elections are distinct. Her executive service ended at year-end 2020; she has chaired the Birzeit trustees since 15 August 2023, not served as university president. Preserve the common 1973 department-foundation and 1986 dean-start dates without imposing a false consensus on doctoral or deanship end dates.
lifeStatusEvidence: The directly read Arabic WAFA report of 20 January 2026 names her among actual participants in the women’s-affairs meeting and reports her remarks as Birzeit trustees chair. The indexed university report of 13 August 2026 additionally describes an academic-cooperation meeting with the Chinese ambassador in that capacity; its body was inaccessible, so it is indexed corroboration rather than a claimed full-source or visual review.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read AUB profile and honorary-degree introduction, relevant PalQuest biography passages, AMAN and ECFR profiles, APF institution history, the 2020 WAFA/Reuters resignation reports, January 2026 Arabic WAFA attendance/remarks passages, and Commons metadata/licence/history. Read indexed university 2023 appointment and August 2026 meeting passages and MIFTAH mission excerpt; those full bodies returned 403 or 502. No full-body claim is made for inaccessible sources.
corrections: Read the AUB honorary-degree profile. It supports BA/MA study at AUB, a University of Virginia PhD, the 1973 English-department foundation and 1991–1993 spokesperson role. Its historical present-tense PLC membership is not a verified 2026 office. It gives a 1986–1990 deanship, while other sources give 1993 or 1995; retain the agreed 1986 start and do not invent a consensus end date.

Read the 28 June 2008 presidential introduction. It specifies English-literature BA/MA degrees, medieval/comparative doctoral work, department chair terms in 1973–1978 and 1981–1984, and 1996–1998 ministerial service. It says the PhD preceded the 1973 return, conflicting with PalQuest’s later thesis-completion account; no definitive doctoral year or pre-return completion is asserted. Its contemporary MIFTAH secretary-general title and PLC office are historical, not current. The reasons given for the 1998 ministerial resignation must not automatically be transplanted to the 2020 PLO resignation.

Read relevant PalQuest biography passages. The precise 8 October 1946 birth in Nablus is explained separately from the family’s Ramallah origin, resolving an otherwise common birthplace confusion. It says she returned in 1973 before completing her dissertation and defended in 1981–1982, unlike AUB’s sequence; omit degree dates. It gives the deanship until 1995, unlike AUB’s 1990 and one university indexed account’s 1993. It corroborates Jerusalem/Third Way parliamentary elections, the 1996–1998 ministry and civic organisations. Its November 2020 resignation shorthand is refined using the dated WAFA statement rather than treated as the end of service. Its 2007 commission name change is distinct from foundation and operational launch.

Read the AMAN board biography. It corroborates her being the first woman elected to the PLO Executive Committee in 2009, re-election in 2018 and departure in 2020. The Jerusalem election in 1996 and Third Way election in 2006 concern the PLC, not PNC or PLO executive seats. It identifies her contribution to ICHR, MIFTAH and AMAN; do not claim all were solely her creations or that the national commission is merely her private NGO. Civic ambitions and organisational biographies are not independent proof of policy outcomes.

Read the ECFR mapping profile. It distinguishes PNC, PLC and PLO executive roles and corroborates the spokesperson and ministerial periods. Its deanship-until-1995 statement is one side of an unresolved chronology; the dossier avoids choosing an unsupported end year. Its PNC statement does not revive a current PLC or executive office. The resignation and reform statement is attributed, not treated as proof of all allegations or the exclusive personal motive for leaving.

Read the APF commission profile. It clearly separates the 1993 presidential decree creating the commission, publication in the Official Gazette in 1995, and commencement of work in early 1994. The decree was issued by Arafat in the capacities specified by the source; do not inaccurately date the institution solely to 1994 or imply that the Palestinian Authority existed in the same form throughout 1993. Ashrawi’s founding role is corroborated by the other institutional biographies, not inferred solely from this commission entry.

Read WAFA’s report dated 9 December 2020, including the resignation-statement chronology: verbal notice on 24 November, written resignation on 26 November, confirmation meeting on 8 December, acceptance on 9 December and departure effective at year-end. November sidebar or current navigation dates are not this article’s date. The public timeline uses acceptance as the dated event and explicitly preserves the later effective end of service. It does not treat 24 November as the written-submission date.

Read the Reuters dispatch carried by Arab News, with Reuters byline and 9 December 2020 publication/update timestamps. It reports the intended year-end departure, political-renewal call, 2009 first election and 2018 re-election. Its earlier account of a deferred acceptance decision is not silently substituted for WAFA’s later report of acceptance that evening. The report says she did not give a specific reason for resignation; reform requests are attributed rather than asserted to be a complete causal explanation. The current site header date is not a new 2026 interview.

Read the Arabic WAFA report dated 20 January 2026, specifically the meeting, attendance and Ashrawi remarks passages. It names her as Birzeit trustees chair, records actual participation and gives her comments on women’s affairs. This is direct recent-activity evidence rather than an upcoming invitation or an old biographical title. Statements by the minister or other participants are not transferred to Ashrawi; the report is not a court determination on the broader conflict. No meeting video was reviewed.

Read indexed university announcement text confirming first-woman trustees chair and the 15 August 2023 start. The page body returned HTTP 403. A separate indexed university announcement identifies the election decision on 3 September 2022 and planned 15 August 2023 inauguration; distinguish decision from taking office. PalQuest and the readable January 2026 WAFA report independently support the chairmanship. University pages give inconsistent deanship end dates of 1993 and 1995, reinforcing the decision to leave the end year unspecified. Chair of the Board of Trustees is not president/rector of the university.

Read the indexed Arabic university report dated 13 August 2026. It identifies Ashrawi as trustees chair and says she met Chinese ambassador Sun Zhen and a delegation to discuss academic and institutional cooperation. The full page returned HTTP 403, so the dossier uses only the indexed event and office, not details beyond the excerpt, actual funding disbursements or completed medical-faculty projects. The university’s publication date is retained; no unseen recording or photo was used to certify appearance. January WAFA remains the directly read recent-activity evidence.

Read the indexed MIFTAH About Us mission excerpt, which gives establishment in Jerusalem in December 1998 and goals of democracy and good governance. The full page returned 502. AUB and AMAN independently corroborate Ashrawi’s founding role. No current secretary-general or executive-management title is asserted from the 2008 introduction, and mission statements are not audited outcomes.

additionalConsulted.access: Indexed text identifies 3 September 2022 election decision and 15 August 2023 start. Full body returned 403; it is not a reviewed board resolution original.
Direct commission page inaccessible. The readable APF institutional profile supports the 1993 decree/1994 operations distinction.
Embassy biography body returned 502. Birth information is supported by the readable PalQuest passage, not claimed from this inaccessible page.
Read metadata and licensing, not image pixels. Correct filename-versus-description date, creator-versus-uploader identity, and capture-versus-upload date distinctions before portrait publication.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review. No original diploma, board minutes, full parliamentary record, full resignation letter original, meeting video, portrait pixels or independent audit of organisational outcomes was reviewed. Some biographical dates conflict; no degree year or deanship end year is asserted. Keep the distinction between directly read bodies and indexed excerpts; refresh current offices and recent developments before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and the English intermediary. Preserve Nablus birth versus Ramallah family; unspecified degree and dean-end years; 1996/2006 PLC versus PNC/PLO executive; first woman executive member versus later first woman trustees chair; 2022 election decision versus 2023 start; trustees chair versus university president; November verbal/written notice versus December acceptance and year-end departure; 1993 commission founding versus 1994 operations; spokesperson versus Oslo signatory; 1998 resignation concerns versus attributed 2020 reform requests; current participation versus historical office.
